history.heading: The Rock
paragraphs: Gibraltar is a small peninsula on the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, dominated by the limestone Rock of Gibraltar. Gorham's Cave, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was one of the last known refuges of Neanderthals. In antiquity the Rock was one of the Pillars of Hercules.
In 711 the Muslim commander Tariq ibn Ziyad landed there to begin the conquest of Iberia, and the name Gibraltar comes from the Arabic Jabal Tariq, "Mount of Tariq". Castile took Gibraltar in 1462.

history.heading: British Gibraltar
paragraphs: An Anglo-Dutch fleet captured Gibraltar in 1704 during the War of the Spanish Succession, and Spain ceded it to Britain in the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht. Spain tried to retake it several times, most notably in the Great Siege of 1779–1783.

Gibraltar became a key British naval base controlling the entrance to the Mediterranean. Spain closed the land border from 1969 to 1985. In referendums in 1967 and 2002, Gibraltarians overwhelmingly voted to remain British.

culture.heading: A mixed heritage
paragraphs: Gibraltarians descend from Genoese, Spanish, British, Maltese, Portuguese, Jewish and other settlers. English is the official language, and many speak Llanito, a mix of Andalusian Spanish and English. Catholic, Anglican, Jewish, Muslim and Hindu communities live side by side.
The Barbary macaques on the Upper Rock are the only wild monkeys in Europe. Local dishes include calentita, a chickpea flatbread.

politics.heading: British Overseas Territory
paragraphs: Gibraltar is a self-governing British Overseas Territory with its own parliament and chief minister; the UK is responsible for defence and foreign affairs. Spain continues to claim sovereignty.
After Brexit, the UK and EU negotiated a treaty, agreed in 2025, to keep the land border with Spain open by bringing Gibraltar into Schengen-style arrangements, with checks at the port and airport.

economy.heading: Services economy
paragraphs: Gibraltar has a prosperous services-based economy, built on online gambling, financial services, shipping services, including ship refuelling, and tourism. Thousands of workers cross daily from Spain.
The Gibraltar pound is at par with the British pound.
